parsed.doc_summary: Berkeley Rent Board page on Measure BB (Nov 2024) amendments to the Rent Ordinance: 5% cap on the Annual General Adjustment for fully covered units, and just-cause eviction changes (nonpayment threshold, lease-breach limits, notice and filing requirements).

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, the yearly rent increase (Annual General Adjustment) follows a CPI-based formula set by the Rent Board but can never exceed 5%. Landlords with banked unused adjustments may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed Nov 2024; the page gives no explicit effective date for the AGA cap. Approximated from the page's Dec 20, 2024 date for tenancy notice requirements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units only: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies begun before 1996, and rooms in single-family homes with 5+ rooms rented separately. Government-subsidized units are now fully or partially covered. Partially covered units (new construction with CO after 1980, most single-family homes and condos) have no rent ceiling.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered units (new construction, most single-family homes and condominiums) and some federally restricted subsidized units are not subject to the rent ceiling.
rules.interaction: Local rule; Berkeley rent control operates alongside the state Tenant Protection Act.
rules.conflict_note: Coverage cutoff approximated from 'built before 1980'. Exact ordinance section not stated on the page.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condominiums are mostly only partially covered
some federally restricted subsidized units are partially covered

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – just cause eviction and notice requirements (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units may evict only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rental debt under one month of HUD Fair Market Rent or for refusing to sign a new fixed-term lease. Lease-breach evictions need a specific notice, substantial actual harm and unreasonable tenant conduct. Termination notices must point to the Rent Board and be filed with it within 3 business days.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance, as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed Nov 2024; the page gives no explicit effective date for the eviction provisions (Dec 20, 2024 appears only for tenant-rights notices).
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no eviction for rent debt under 1 month FMR
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered units, including government-owned or subsidized units now registered with the Rent Board.
rules.exemptions: Exempt units; units where tenant shares kitchen or bath with a landlord who lived there before the tenancy.
rules.interaction: Local just-cause rule governs for covered units.

unverifiable_exemptions: units where tenant shares kitchen or bath with a landlord who lived there first
